static_traits.name: Ai Lin
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive colleague group, but has not yet shared specific concerns about Student grades with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation, able to Reflect on one's own cognitive patterns; tense, Anxious tone when talking about Student grades

basic_info.main_problem: I keep worrying my Students may not perform well at school, though I love teaching and believe in their potential.
basic_info.core_demands: Escalating worries about Student academic performance prompted me to seek counseling, hoping to resolve this persistent distress.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on students' grades
I am an incompetent teacher (if Students fail it proves I fail)

special_situations.event: During Exam period or when receiving Student grade feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If Students perform poorly, it means my teaching failed; I am an incompetent Teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Implementing new teaching strategies and seeking colleagues' advice to improve Student grades
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not do well on the exam; It is all my fault

special_situations.event: In classroom assessments and parent-teacher meeting settings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If parents or evaluations show Students have problems, I will be seen as a failure and incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-focusing on Students' difficulties during evaluations, anticipating the worst outcome in advance and preparing doubly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will fail the exam; Parent-teacher meeting will think I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Seeing a Student momentarily struggle with Learning in class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a Student struggles now, they will surely fail in the end and prove I did not teach well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately blames herself and tries extra tutoring or quickly adjusting the teaching plan
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He is going to fail, because I did not teach well

special_situations.event: Still repeatedly ruminating on Student academic performance during weekend hiking leisure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even during rest time one must constantly watch Student grades, or problems will arise
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent rumination, difficulty relaxing, tries to gain a sense of control through thinking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I relax, Students' grades will get worse

core_conflict.wish: Longing for Students to succeed, and to be recognized as a competent, influential Teacher
core_conflict.fear: Fear that poor Student performance means one's own failure, leading to negation and criticism from parents or colleagues
defense_goal: Avoids being criticized or judged through continuous monitoring and self-pressure
Focuses attention on problems and worst-case scenarios to gain a sense of control

object_relations.self_representation: A responsible, self-blame-prone Teacher (viewing Students' failure as one's own failure)
object_relations.object_representation: Parents / colleagues are harsh judges who may negate oneself at any time

object_relations.self_representation: Helper who must always care for and be responsible for others
object_relations.object_representation: Students are fragile, may fail, objects needing one's rescue and support

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out she equates Student grades with her own ability and worth
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to interpret external evaluations as accusations of self-incompetence, fearing negation (transference: self-criticism intensifying)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, validating tone, first Empathizing with the sense of responsibility and Anxiety, then using open-ended Questioning to Guidance distinguishing Student outcomes from self-worth, avoiding blame; slowing pace, encouraging recall of concrete facts and positive evidence.

manifestations: Strong responsibility and control needs compressing personal Freedom and leisure experience
Weekend hiking also occupied by worries about Student grades, Difficulty relaxing
Although having a supportive colleague network, not yet sharing specific worries, tending to bear pressure alone

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Viewing Student grades as the absolute measure of self-worth ('I must make them all do well')
Uses external expectations as the sole basis for self-evaluation during assessments and parent meetings

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on.
manifestations: Repeated self-blame, viewing Students' failure as one's own failure
When facing negative feedback, over-examines self, raises inner standards, and intensifies pressure

positive_force: Passionate about teaching and firmly believing in Student potential
Actively tries new teaching strategies and seeks advice from colleagues
Once gained some stress-relief experience through weekend hiking
negative_force: Catastrophizing and future-predicting cognitive patterns intensifying Anxiety
Strongly binding Student grades to self-worth, forming Excessive self-blame
Persistent worry intrudes into daily life, weakening job satisfaction and quality of leisure

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent worry and Anticipatory Anxiety (repeatedly predicting Students will fail)
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly binding Students' performance to self-worth, and interpreting current difficulties through catastrophizing and predicting the future
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control through excessive worry, avoiding the risk of being criticized or seen as incompetent
target_behavior.consequence: Rising Anxiety levels, Decreased job satisfaction, weekend leisure disrupted

target_behavior.behavior: Unable to relax in leisure settings, continuously ruminating on Student grade issues
antecedent: Thinking about the upcoming evaluation or parent-teacher meeting
target_behavior.core_reason: Believing one must keep watching and controlling Student performance even while resting, or worse outcomes will occur (control fallacy)
target_behavior.function: Trying to maintain a sense of control over outcomes, reducing uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Leisure experience ruined, insufficient physical and mental Recovery, overall Decreased quality of life
